chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Manṣūr Buzurj, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Do not let one who is free-handed in shedding blood deceive you, for indeed he has, with Allah, a killer that does not die.”
They said, “O Messenger of Allah, and what is a killer that does not die?” He said: “The Fire.”

key_terms.النَّارُ: the Fire, meaning hellfire as divine punishment
key_terms.رَحْبُ الذِّرَاعَيْنِ بِالدَّمِ: being unrestrained and free-handed in shedding blood
key_terms.قَاتِلًا لَا يَمُوتُ: an enduring destroyer or punishment that does not cease

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the punishment for shedding blood unjustly?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against being impressed by a person who sheds blood with apparent power or impunity. It teaches that unlawful killing carries an enduring divine punishment, identified here as the Fire. The narration strongly condemns bloodshed and directs attention to accountability in the afterlife.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5152 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mansur Buzurj from Abu Hamzah Al-Thumali from Imam Ali ibn Al-Hussain (as), who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (swt) said:
"Do not be deceived by one who freely sheds blood, for indeed, he has a killer appointed for him by Allah (swt) who does not die."

They asked: "O' Messenger of Allah (swt), and what is the killer that does not die?"
Prophet (sw) said: "The Fire."
